audit: No novel gene-diagnosis association met the bar for a paper; every claim reported is, to my knowledge, already established. The four strongest 'novel-looking' signals were deliberately excluded after scrutiny: ARID1B in 'Rhabdomyosarcoma, NOS' (16/66 vs 7/1647, p~1e-18), ZMYM3 in 'Glioma, malignant' (20/166), ASXL1 in 'Medulloblastoma, NOS' (17/212) and PIK3R1 in 'Pilocytic astrocytoma' (30/168). Each is made of scattered, non-recurrent, mostly missense changes with no hotspot and no truncation enrichment (unlike true drivers here such as FGFR4 V550L, FBXW7 R505C, KMT2D truncations); ARID1B appears in 0/75 embryonal and 0/30 alveolar RMS despite 'RMS, NOS' being a mix of those; ZMYM3 is absent from Glioblastoma and Astrocytoma, NOS; PIK3R1 missense variants are often the only mutation in tumors carrying 1-3 mutations and sit alongside canonical MAPK drivers. This pattern looks like a label-specific batch, calling or curation artifact, not biology, and I would not headline it without orthogonal validation. Other concerns: 18 hypermutated tumors (up to 15,731 mutations, mostly 'Glioma, malignant', likely MMR/POLE-deficient) were excluded because they inflate every gene's count; diagnosis labels are heterogeneous and overlapping (NOS categories, 81 'missing', 25 'Unknown', many classes with <10 cases), so small-class estimates are imprecise; WES calls miss fusions and copy-number events (e.g. KIAA1549-BRAF in pilocytic astrocytoma, PAX3/7-FOXO1 in ARMS, SMARCB1 deletions), so frequencies understate driver prevalence; protein coordinates follow a non-legacy transcript (BRAF V640E = V600E; H3-3A K28M = K27M); and with ~1,000+ diagnosis-gene tests, many nominal p<1e-3 hits in small classes (e.g. CYP4F8, RRAS2, NOS3) are expected by chance. I recognise the renewal needs novelty, but reporting the excluded signals as new findings would risk not replicating.
methods: Each case was coded per gene as mutated or not, counting any non-synonymous somatic mutation. I excluded hypermutated tumors (>200 mutated genes; 18 cases). For each diagnosis label with 3 or more cases, and each gene mutated in at least 2 of its cases, I ran a one-sided Fisher exact test of that diagnosis against all other cases (stdlib hypergeometric), and ranked results with a Benjamini-Hochberg-style correction. I screened the top hits for artifacts: hotspot recurrence, truncating fraction, consistency across related diagnosis labels, co-occurrence with canonical drivers, and hypermutator or duplicate-sample effects (no duplicate samples were found). I also checked established diagnosis-driver pairs directly. expected_frequency is the observed rate shrunk slightly toward the background rate, and probability combines statistical strength, class size and prior biological plausibility.
